concept.name: Market-value-to-realized-value ratio
concept.definition: MVRV (market-value-to-realized-value) is the ratio of an asset's market capitalization to its realized capitalization, comparing the market's current valuation to the aggregate on-chain cost basis.
concept.intuition: MVRV asks whether holders are, on average, sitting on big paper gains (ratio high, temptation to sell) or paper losses (ratio low, capitulation territory).
concept.mechanics: MVRV = market cap / realized cap. Values >1 mean the average holder is in profit; extremes (>~3.5 historically for BTC) marked late-stage bull markets, while MVRV <1 — price below aggregate cost basis — historically coincided with bear-market bottoms and accumulation zones. It functions as a mean-reversion gauge with realized cap as the mean.
concept.failure_modes: As market structure matures (ETFs, derivatives, longer holder memory), historical thresholds like 3.5 drift and should not be applied mechanically; exchange-internal coin movements distort realized cap and hence the ratio.
concept.misconceptions: MVRV is not a timing tool for entries and exits — it identifies valuation regimes, and markets can stay 'overvalued' or 'undervalued' for months. It is an analytical framework from on-chain data, not a proven predictive law.
concept.example: With BTC market cap at $1.2T and realized cap at $500B, MVRV = 2.4 — deep aggregate profit historically associated with elevated distribution risk, though below the >3.5 extremes of prior cycle tops.
